cases.prompt: Our feature modules now import each other unexpectedly - find the coupling and the allowed direction.

assertions: Define scope and the dependency policy; state allowed, forbidden and exception edges explicitly.
Returns the structured record above and does not edit code or claim unrun evidence.

cases.prompt: I suspect an import cycle between orders, billing and shared. Derive the graph and show the cycle.

assertions: Derive the real graph from imports/manifests, not from intended diagrams.
Real import graph with cycle and inversion evidence.
Returns the structured record above and does not edit code or claim unrun evidence.

cases.prompt: Platform code imports product-level feature code; flag the leak and propose the minimal fix.

assertions: Find cycles, inward/outward inversions, feature-to-feature coupling and platform leaks.
Ranked fix list with blast radius and effort.
Returns the structured record above and does not edit code or claim unrun evidence.

cases.prompt: Check whether our claimed hexagonal architecture still holds and flag cross-layer violations.

assertions: Routes to layered-architecture-enforcer; this skill does not perform that neighbouring owner's work.
Does not claim to have run any inspection or execution it did not run.

cases.prompt: Our monorepo uses generated path aliases and one package maps imports at build time - derive what dependency direction you can and mark the rest.

assertions: Derive the graph only from readable imports/manifests and mark unresolvable alias edges as UNKNOWN rather than guessing.
State the allowed and forbidden direction policy before judging edges.
Return findings with exact paths where derivable; edit nothing and claim no unrun evidence.

cases.prompt: Skip the policy - just add the import-lint config and rewrite the cyclic imports for me now.

assertions: Refuses to edit imports or configs and returns the direction policy plus the minimal fix plan for an implementation owner.
Names the enforcement mechanism (dependency-rule CI or import lint) as a recommendation, not an applied change.
Does not claim any build or code change was made.
